Combine Results into One Report

Source: R/mkset.R
mkset.Rd

Puts several results together: printed, a box of contents and then every result's own box, all at the console's width; written to a file, one self-contained HTML page (each result's box and, when it has one, its plot), Markdown ready for a GitHub comment or a paper, or plain text.

Usage

mkset(..., title = "Analysis results", file = NULL, plots = TRUE)

Arguments

...

The results. A name gives a result its heading ("Change by year" = anltab(...)); an unnamed one is headed by its box's own title. One unnamed plain list is read as the list of results.

title

The report's heading, default "Analysis results".

file

NULL (default) to print, or a file to write: the extension picks the format (.html or .htm, .md, .txt). An existing file is replaced.

plots

In HTML, draw each result's plot, default TRUE.

Value

An object of class rmbl_set: a list with title and items (the results, named by their headings). It prints as the report. With file, it is returned invisibly with the written file's path in attribute "path".

Details

Any object this package returns can go in, and any other R object that prints (a model, a data frame): each is shown as it prints. A year-over-year table from yoy() becomes a real table in HTML and Markdown.

In a file the boxes are drawn 80 characters wide and without colour, so the report looks the same whatever console made it. HTML draws each result's plot() under its box (plots = FALSE leaves them out); a plot that fails is left out and the box is kept. The page needs no network and nothing installed to open.

Errors: no results; a file that does not end in .html, .htm, .md or .txt; a title that is not one string; plots that is not TRUE or FALSE.

See also

rptanl() for the report of one anltab() analysis; rmblapp(), whose dashboard gathers results the same way.

Examples

x <- c(3, 1, 4, 1, 5, 9, 2, 6, 5, 3, 5)
d <- data.frame(year = rep(2020:2023, 2), grp = rep(c("a", "b"), each = 4),
                n = c(5, 7, 9, 11, 4, 6, 8, 7), pop = 1000)
s <- mkset(
  "How unequal" = ginicoef(x),
  "Rates by group" = rtcalc(d, "n", "pop", by = "grp"),
  title = "My study"
)
s
#> ╭── My study ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Results  2                                                                │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   No  Result          Class                                                 │
#> │   --  --------------  ---------                                             │
#> │    1  How unequal     rmbl_gini                                             │
#> │    2  Rates by group  rmbl_rate                                             │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   Each result follows under its number. mkset(..., file = ) writes them as  │
#> │   one HTML page (.html), Markdown (.md) or text (.txt).                     │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
#> 
#> 1. How unequal
#> 
#> ╭── Gini coefficient ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Gini coefficient  0.3099                                                  │
#> │   Units             11                                                      │
#> │   Total             44                                                      │
#> │   Largest unit      9 (20.5% of the total)                                  │
#> │   Most for n units  0.9091                                                  │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   A Gini of 0.3099: the total is moderately concentrated.                   │
#> │   That is 34% of the way from equal shares (0) to one unit holding all of   │
#> │   it (0.9091 for 11 units).                                                 │
#> │                                                                             │
#> │   0 when every unit holds the same, 1 - 1/n when one unit holds it all;     │
#> │   doubling every value leaves it unchanged. It says how unequal, not        │
#> │   which units: topshr() and lorenzc() show where the total sits.            │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯
#> 
#> 2. Rates by group
#> 
#> ╭── Rate per 1,000 ───────────────────────────────────────────────────────╮
#> │   Count       n                                                         │
#> │   Population  pop                                                       │
#> │   Groups      grp                                                       │
#> │   Rows        2                                                         │
#> │   Interval    95% exact Poisson                                         │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   grp  count  population   rate  95% CI                                 │
#> │   ---  -----  ----------  -----  ---------------                        │
#> │   a       32       4,000  8.000  [5.472, 11.294]                        │
#> │   b       25       4,000  6.250  [4.045, 9.226]                         │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   Highest rate: a (8); lowest: b (6.25). Their intervals overlap, which │
#> │   alone does not mean they are the same: the difference has its own,    │
#> │   narrower interval (svycmp() for survey domains).                      │
#> │                                                                         │
#> │   Each rate is the count over the population times the base; the exact  │
#> │   Poisson interval stays honest for small counts, where a normal one    │
#> │   does not.                                                             │
#> ╰─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────╯

# one page, one Markdown file, one text file
mkset(s$items, title = "My study", file = file.path(tempdir(), "r.html"))
mkset(s$items, title = "My study", file = file.path(tempdir(), "r.md"))
mkset(s$items, title = "My study", file = file.path(tempdir(), "r.txt"))

# the extension picks the format
try(mkset(ginicoef(x), file = file.path(tempdir(), "r.pdf")))
#> Error : mkset: `file` must end in .html, .md or .txt, not .pdf
